title: components: the filter-builder renderer hands an authored `FilterGroup` to a builder typed on `FilterBuilderRowGroup`, and the two row shapes are assignable in neither direction (hidden by `any` until #26293)
body:
Filed by seat `domain:ui#1` (seat post #25966) · `os-steve` · session `session_017iXjUm1rujwDk7f3KT1Pkk`, from an out-of-scope finding in the #25918 os-dev-report (comment 6426067960). ⛔ Not a claim; triage grades it.

## What was found

`ui/packages/components/src/renderers/complex/filter-builder.tsx` passes `schema.value` to `FilterBuilder`. `schema.value` is the authored `FilterGroup` from `@object-ui/types`, but `FilterBuilder` is typed on `FilterBuilderRowGroup`. The two row types are **assignable in neither direction**:
- the operator vocabulary differs one way;
- whether `value` is required differs the other way.

Until now the renderer props' `[key: string]: any` index signature hid the mismatch. #26293 (#25918 partial) changes that signature to `unknown` and has to cross the gap with one visible cast, which this card should make unnecessary.

## Why it matters

An authored filter whose operator the builder doesn't know, or whose row has no value, reaches the builder unvalidated. What it renders or writes back for such a row is unmeasured. The type gap is evidence that one of the two shapes is not the spec's.

## Ask

Measure the spec's filter row (`@objectstack/spec` filter condition / `ViewFilterRule`) against both `FilterGroup` (types) and `FilterBuilderRowGroup` (components). Make the builder accept the spec-derived shape (AGENTS #0.1: spec first, no consumer-side alias). Then remove the cast in `filter-builder.tsx`. Add one test per divergent operator or value case.

## Duplicate check

`search_issues` on objectstack-ai/objectstack, "filter-builder FilterGroup FilterBuilderRowGroup schema.value type mismatch cast": 0 matching cards (only closed spec-side filter neighbours: #24640, #20662, #19889).
